body.text: // Ārya amoghapāśahṛdaya nāma mahāyānasūtram //
body.translated_text: The Noble <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s> (Heart of the Infallible Lasso), a <s>Mahāyāna sūtra</s>.

body.text: // om namo bhagavate ārya amoghapāśahṛdaya //
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. Homage to the Blessed Noble <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s>.

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam - ekasmin samaye bhagavān potalake parvate viharati sma / āryāvalokiteśvarasya bhavane anekaśālatamālacampakāśokātimuktaka nānāvṛkṣasamalaṅkṛte / mahatābhikṣusaṃghena sārddhamaṣṭādaśabhirbhikṣusahasraiḥ / navanavatibhiśca bodhisattvakoṭiniyutaśatasahasraiḥ / anekaiśca śuddhāvāsikairdevaputra koṭiniyutaśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛta īśvaramaheśvarabrahmakāyikān devaputrān adhikṛtya dharma deśayati sma /
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling on Mount <s>Potalaka</s>, in the abode of the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, adorned with many <s>śāla</s> trees, <s>tamāla</s> trees, <s>campaka</s> trees, <s>aśoka</s> trees, <s>atimuktaka</s> vines, and various other trees. He was surrounded and honored by a great assembly of monks—eighteen thousand <s>bhikṣus</s>—and ninety-nine hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and many hundred thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>devaputras</s> (divine sons) from the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes). He was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> with reference to <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, and the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> <s>devaputras</s>.

body.text: atha khalu āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattva utthāyāsanādekāṃ samuttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavān tenāñjaliṃ kṛtvā praṇamya prahasitavadano bhūtvā bhagavantametadavocat /
body.translated_text: Then the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavat</s>, bowing, and with a smiling face, spoke thus to the <s>Bhagavat</s>:

body.text: asti mama bhagavan amoghapāśarājannāma hṛdayaṃ yanmayā pūrvvamekanavatime kalpe vilokitāyāṃ lokadhātau lokendrarājo nāma tathāgatasya sakāśādudgṛhītam / yena bhagavannīśvara devamaheśvara devaputrapramukhāni vahūni śuddhāvāsikāyika devaputrapramukhānyanekadevaputraśatasahasrāṇi samādāpitānyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau asaṃmohajñānavyūhapramukhāni ca mayā daśasamādhiśatasahasrāṇi pratilabdhāni / yasmiṃśca puna rbhagavan pṛthivī pradeśe idamamoghapāśahṛdayaṃ pracaret / veditavyaṃ bhagavan stasmin pṛthivīpradeśe īśvaramaheśvarabrahmakāyikapramukhāni dvādaśadevaputraśatasahasrāṇi rakṣāvaraṇaguptaye sthāsyanti / caityasammato bhagavan pṛthivīpradeśo bhaviṣyati / yatredam amoghapāśahṛdayaṃ pracariṣyati / aneka buddhakoṭi niyutaśatasahasrāvaropitakuśalamūlāste bhagavan sattvā bhaviṣyanti / ya idaṃmadīyam amoghapāśahṛdayaṃ śroṣyanti / yaḥ kaścidabhagavan kilviṣakārī syāt / sarvvapāpāspadaḥ pāpadharmmasamācāraḥ āryāpavādakaḥ sadharmapratikṣepakaḥ / avīciparāyaṇaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattva ārya śrāvakapratyeka buddha pratikṣepakaḥ / sa cedviprasāraṃ gacchet / āpabhyāṃ samvaramāpadyate /
body.translated_text: 'O <s>Bhagavat</s>, I have a <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart-dhāraṇī) called <s>Amoghapāśarāja</s> (King of the Infallible Lasso), which I received long ago, in the ninety-first <s>kalpa</s> (aeon), from the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Lokendrarāja</s> in the world-system called <s>Vilokitā</s>. By it, O <s>Bhagavat</s>, many hundred thousands of <s>devaputras</s> headed by <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, and the <s>Śuddhāvāsika</s> <s>devaputras</s> have been inspired toward unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), and I have obtained a hundred thousand collections of ten <s>samādhis</s> headed by the array of non-deluded knowledge (<s>asaṃmoha-jñāna-vyūha</s>). And furthermore, O <s>Bhagavat</s>, in whatever region of the earth this <s>Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya</s> shall be practiced—it should be known, O <s>Bhagavat</s>, that in that region twelve hundred thousand <s>devaputras</s> headed by <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, and the <s>Brahmakāyikas</s> will stand guard for protection and shelter. O <s>Bhagavat</s>, the region of the earth where this <s>Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya</s> shall be practiced will become [as sacred as] a <s>caitya</s> (shrine). O <s>Bhagavat</s>, those beings who shall hear this <s>Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya</s> of mine will have wholesome roots planted with many hundred thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>. O <s>Bhagavat</s>, whoever may be a wrongdoer, a resort of all sins, one who practices sinful conduct, a slanderer of the Noble Ones, a rejecter of the True <s>Dharma</s>, one destined for <s>Avīci</s> (the lowest hell), a rejecter of all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, Noble <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>—if he should feel remorse and undertake the restraints [of this dhāraṇī],'

body.text: yasyaiva tāvadbhagavan ekopavāho jāpena ihaiva janmani tatkarma viśudhyati / parikṣayaṃ gacchati vāntibhavati / ekāhikena jvareṇa dvāhikena trāhikena vā cāturthikena vā evaṃ saptāhi kena vā jvareṇa / akṣiśūlena vā karṇa śūlena vā nāsāśūlena vā / daṃtoṣṭhaśūlena vā jivhāśūlena vā / tāluśūlena va hṛdayaśūlena va udaraśūlena vā pārśvaśūlena vā kaṭiśūlena vā aṅgapratyaṅgaśūlena vā arśagrahaṇīśūlena vā atisāreṇa vā hastapādaveda nayā vā śirorujā va valāhakaścitra kuṣṭhaśriyarccikā kirīmalohaliṅgalagrahabhagaṇḍalavisphoṭaka apasmāra kākhorddakhyai rvākṛtāpakṛtyaivā vaṃndhanaṃ vandhanatāḍana tarjjanā bhūtākhyanairvā / saṃkṣepato bhagavan kāyapīḍayāvā cittapīḍayā vā dusvapnadarśanaṃ vā tatkarmaparikṣayaṃ gacchati / paryavadānaṃ gacchati / prāgeva śuddhasattvānāṃ śraddhādhimuktikānāṃ yadi bhagavan catasraḥ pariṣadaścatvāro varṇā yāmā yā sāthenāpiya idamadiyama amoghapāśahṛdayaṃ śroṣyanti / udgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti likhiṣyanti likhāpayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti anyeṣāṃ sattvānāṃ śrāvayiṣyanti antastiryagyonigatānāṃ vā sattvānāṃ karṇāpūṭasthitvā karṇajāpaṃ dāṣyanti / imānica mantrapadāni cintayiṣyanti / apratikṣepataḥ asaṃprabhavataḥ / aviraṃgamataḥ akaraṇataḥ niḥkleśataḥ samacintākṣepakaḥ virahitapaṃcaskandhasvabhāvena / anena yogena buddhānusmṛtiḥ karttavyā / teṣāṃ daśabhyo digbhyo buddhasahasraṃ saṃmukhaṃ darśanaṃ kariṣyanti / atyayadeśanāṃ ca kariṣyanti / peyālaṃ / yāvatpustakalikhitaṃ vā kṛtvā gṛhe sthāpayiṣyanti / kiṃ bahunā bhagavannanyonyaśraddhayā vā śroṣyanti / svāmibhayena vā parānuttarā vā / uccagdhanahetunā vā śroṣyanti / jñātavyamiti bhagavan paṇḍite nāryāvalokiteśvarasyānubhāvena teṣāṃ karṇapuṭe śabdo niścarati /
body.translated_text: O Blessed One, by even a single day's observance with recitation, in this very life that <s>karma</s> is purified, comes to exhaustion, or is consumed. Whether it be a daily fever, a two-day fever, a three-day fever, or a four-day fever, or even a seven-day fever; whether it be eye-pain, ear-pain, nose-pain, tooth-and-lip-pain, tongue-pain, palate-pain, heart-pain, stomach-pain, side-pain, hip-pain, pain of limbs and minor limbs, pain of hemorrhoids and intestinal ailments, dysentery, affliction of the hands and feet, headache, skin diseases, leprosy, eczema, scrofula, ulcers, fistula, boils, epilepsy, poisoning, sorcery, hostile rites, binding, beating, threats, or afflictions by spirits — in short, O Blessed One, whether bodily affliction, mental affliction, or the seeing of evil dreams — that <s>karma</s> comes to exhaustion and purification. How much more so for beings of pure nature and faithful disposition! O Blessed One, if the four assemblies, the four castes, or any others, even those of evil intent, shall hear this <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s> (the Heart of the Unfailing Noose), shall take it up, retain it, recite it, write it, cause it to be written, master it, and cause other beings to hear it — even for beings born in the animal realm, standing at their ear and giving an ear-whispered recitation — and shall contemplate these <s>mantra</s>-words: without rejection, without confusion, without separation, without inaction, free from defilements, with equanimous contemplation, devoid of the inherent nature of the five aggregates (<s>pañcaskandha</s>) — by this practice, <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> (recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>) should be performed. For them, thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> from the ten directions shall grant a face-to-face vision. And they shall perform confession of transgressions. [And so forth.] Up to: having made a written copy, they shall keep it in their homes. What more need be said, O Blessed One? Even those who hear it merely through mutual faith, or through fear of a master, or from a supreme [motive], or for the sake of gaining wealth — it should be known, O Blessed One, by the wise, that through the power of the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the sound enters their ears.

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma bhagavan kaścidevapurūṣaścandanaṃ vā kapūraṃ vā kasturikaṃ vā ākṛṣya paribhāṣya śilāyāṃ vā piṣṭvā ātmānaṃ lepayet / na tasya candanasya kapurakasya kasturikāyā vā / evaṃ bhavatyanāmākṛṣṭaḥ paribhāṣito vā gandhenāti kramiṣyāmiti / api ca gandha eva sa eva meva bhagavanidaṃ madoyamamoghapāśannāma hṛdayaṃ yaḥ kaścidudgrāsdya ullāpya / peyālaṃ / yāvatmāyāśabdenāpātheye nāpi pūjayeta / teṣāṃ bhagavana khakānāṃ sattvānāṃ sa eva kuśalamūla heturbhaviṣyati / yatra yatropapatsyante tatra tatra virahitāśca bhaviṣyanti / śīlasamādhiprajñāpuṇyasambhāragandhena śīlasaugandhikameva karoti / yaḥ kaścit bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bhikṣurvā bhikṣuṇī vā upāśako vā upāśikā vā / tadanyo vā kaścidamoghapāśahṛdayamuddisyaśuklāṣṭamyāmupavāsaṃ kuryāt / saptavārān amoghapāśahṛdayamanālapataḥ āvarttayet / tasya bhagavan dṛṣṭa eva dharmma viśatiranuśaṃsaḥ pratikāṃkṣitavyāḥ / katame viṃśatiḥ? yaduta rogāścāsya kāyenopapatsyante / utpanāścāsya rogāḥ karmmavaśena śīghraṃ prasamaṃ yāsyanti / snigdhamanojñasāślakṣlagātra śca bhaviṣyati / vahujanapriyaśca bhaviṣyati / guptendriryā 'rtha pratilambhaśca bhaviṣyati / utpannāṃśca 'rthemyo pratilapsyate /
body.translated_text: Just as, O Blessed One, a certain person, having obtained sandalwood, camphor, or musk, having ground and mixed it on a stone, would anoint himself — that sandalwood, camphor, or musk does not think 'I have been obtained and mixed, and I shall surpass with my fragrance' — yet the fragrance itself pervades. Even so, O Blessed One, this is my <s>Amoghapāśa</s>-named <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart-dhāraṇī). Whoever shall take it up and recite it — [and so forth] — up to: even if one should not worship it properly, or [recite it] with deceitful words — for those ignorant beings, O Blessed One, it shall become the very cause of their roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>). Wherever they shall be reborn, there they shall be endowed [with merit]. It produces the fragrance of moral conduct through the accumulation of merit consisting of <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). O Blessed One, whatever son or daughter of good family, <s>bhikṣu</s> or <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, <s>upāsaka</s> or <s>upāsikā</s>, or anyone else, who, dedicating themselves to the <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s>, shall observe the <s>upavāsa</s> (fasting vow) on the eighth day of the bright fortnight and recite the <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s> seven times without interruption — for them, O Blessed One, twenty benefits are to be expected in this very life. What are the twenty? Namely: diseases shall not arise in their body; and diseases that have already arisen through the force of <s>karma</s> shall quickly come to cessation; they shall have smooth, pleasant, and delicate limbs; they shall be dear to many people; they shall have guarded faculties and obtain wealth; and they shall acquire whatever wealth has arisen.

body.text: agninā dahyante nodakena hrīyante / rājā na śaknoti manasā pāpahartum / karmāntaścāsya sphītā bhavanti / nāśaninodakabhayaṃ bhaviṣyati / na vātavṛṣṭibhayaṃ bhaviṣyati / saptavārāna amoghapāśahṛdayena bhasmodakaṃ vā parijapya digavidigūrddhaṃ ca kṣetrasya vandho dātavya / sarvopadravā upaśamisyati / na ojohārā ojopaharantuṃ śaknuvanti / sarvasattvānāṃ priyo bhaviṣyati / mana āpaśca bhaviṣyati / śatru bhayaṃ cāsya na bhaviṣyati / utpannacāsya śatru bhayaṃ śīghraṃ praśamaṃ yāsyati / na cāsya manuṣyabhayaṃ bhaviṣyati / na kākhorddhabhayaṃ na cāsya ḍākinībhayaṃ na cāsya tīvrāḥ kleśopakleśā bhaviṣyanti / nāgninā na śastreṇaviṣeṇaṃ kālaṃ kariṣyanti / devatācāsya satata samitaṃ rakṣāvaraṇaguptaye sthāsyanti / yatra yatropapatsyante tatra tatrāvirahitaśca bhaviṣyati maitrīkarūṇāmuditopekṣāyāḥ / ime viśatiranuśaṃsāḥ pratikāṃkṣitavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: [They] are not burned by fire, nor carried away by water. A king is not able to steal [their possessions] by thought. And their enterprises become prosperous. There will be no danger from thunderbolts or water. There will be no danger from wind and rain. Having recited the <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s> seven times over ash-water, protection should be given to the field in the directions, intermediate directions, and above. All calamities will be pacified. <s>Ojohārās</s> (vitality-stealers) are unable to steal [their] vitality. One will become dear to all beings. One will become agreeable in mind and appearance. There will be no danger from enemies. And any danger from enemies that has arisen will quickly be pacified. There will be no danger from humans. No danger from <s>kākhordas</s> (sorcerers). No danger from <s>ḍākinīs</s>. Nor will there be intense <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) or secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśa</s>). One will not meet death by fire, by weapons, or by poison. And <s>devatās</s> (deities) will constantly stand guard for protection, shelter, and safekeeping. Wherever one is reborn, there one will never be separated from <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity). These twenty benefits are to be expected.

body.text: aparānaṣṭau dharmān pratilapsyante / katamānaṣṭau? maraṇakālasamaye āryāvalokiteśvaro bhikṣurūpeṇa sammukhadarśanaṃ dāsyanti // 1 // sasukhenakālaṃ kariṣyati // 2 // na bhrāntadṛṣṭirbhaviṣyati // 3 // na hastavikṣepaṃ kariṣyati // 4 // na pādavikṣepaṃ kariṣyati // 5 // noccāraṇannaprasrāvaṃ na cārūḍha kālaṃ kariṣyati // 6 // sukhapratiṣṭhita smṛtirbhaviṣyati // 7 // nādhomukhakālaṃ kariṣyati // 8 // maraṇakāle akṣayapratibhānaṃ cāsya bhaviṣyati / yatra cāsya buddhakṣetre praṇidhistatropapattirbhaviṣyati / avirahitaśca kalyānamitrā bhaviṣyanti / dine dine triṣkālaṃ triṇi vārān pariāvarttayitavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, one will obtain eight <s>dharmas</s> (qualities). Which eight? (1) At the time of death, the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, in the form of a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), will grant a direct vision face-to-face. (2) One will die in comfort. (3) One's vision will not be confused. (4) One will not make agitated movements of the hands. (5) One will not make agitated movements of the feet. (6) One will not die while passing excrement, urinating, or in a raised position. (7) One's mindfulness will be well-established and at ease. (8) One will not die face-downward. At the time of death, one will have inexhaustible eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>). And in whichever <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field) one has made a vow (<s>praṇidhi</s>), there one will be reborn. And one will never be separated from virtuous spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>). Three times daily, three times, [this dhāraṇī] should be recited.

body.text: madyamāṃsapālāṇḍuguṃ kṛtocchiṣṭhaṃ viṣayardhinājyate varjjayitavyaṃ / ayaṃ cāmoghapāśahṛdayo nāma dharmaparyāyaḥ sarvasatvānāṃ ca valāvalaṃ jñātvā śrāvayitavyam / ācāryamuṣṭirna karttavyāḥ / yasmādvigato malamātsaryobyāpagato bodhisattvā bhavanti / satvānāmārthakaraṇena buddhabodhiḥ prāpyate bodhirityucyate prajñāsattva ityupāyaḥ // etau dvaudharmmī sattvārthe naiva prāpyate / sacetme bhagavan anujānī yāt / idaṃ hṛdayaṃ tathāgatasya purataḥ kīrtta yeyaṃ catasṛṇāṃ parṣadām arthāyabodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocata / bhāṣatvaṃ śuddhasattvāya yasyedāniṃ kāla manyase /
body.translated_text: Meat, liquor, onions, garlic, leftover food, and sense-pleasures should be avoided. And this <s>Dharma</s> discourse called the <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s> should be taught to all beings, having discerned their spiritual capacity. The teacher's closed fist [of secrecy] should not be employed, because <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are those who are free from the stain of jealousy and ill-will. <s>Buddhabodhi</s> (the awakening of a Buddha) is attained through working for the benefit of beings. What is called <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) is <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom); what is called <s>sattva</s> (being) is <s>upāya</s> (skillful means). These two <s>dharmas</s> are never obtained [except] for the welfare of beings. 'If the <s>Bhagavat</s> would give me permission, I would proclaim this <s>hṛdaya</s> before the <s>Tathāgata</s>, for the benefit of the four assemblies (<s>parṣad</s>)' — thus he addressed the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>. [The Buddha said:] 'Speak, O pure-minded one, if you now deem this the proper time.'

body.text: anumoditaṃ tathāgatena paścime kāle paścime samaye bodhisattvayānikānāṃ pitṛkāryakariṣyanti / atha khalu āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nibhiṣanayano bhūtvā bhagavanta metadabocata / śṛṇu me bhagavan sarvabodhisattva namaskṛtamidaṃ vimokṣamukhamaṇḍalaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya // nāmastryadhvānugatapratiṣṭhitebhya sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyo namaḥ pratyekabuddhāryaśrāvaka saṃghebhyo 'tītānāgatapratyutpannebhyo namaḥ samyaggatānāṃ / namaḥ samyakapratipannānā / namaḥ śāradvatīputrāya mahādānapataye / namaḥ āryāmaitreyapramukhebhyo mahābodhisattvasaṃghebhyaḥ namo 'tītānāgatapratyutpannebhyastathāgatebhyo 'rhatsaṃmyakasambuddhebhyo / namaḥ suvarṇavarṇaprabhāya tathāagatāya / namaḥ siṃhavikrīḍītarājāya tathāgatāya / namo vipaśvine tathāgatāya / namaḥ śikhine tathāgatāya arhate samyak sambuddhāya / namo viśvabhuve tathāgatāya / namaḥ krakucchandāya tathāgatāya / namaḥ kanakamunaye tathagatāya / namaḥ kāśyapāya tathāgatāyā / namaḥ śākyamunaye tathagatāryārhate samyaksambuddhāya // tadyathā //
body.translated_text: Approved by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, in the last time, in the last age, they shall perform the ancestral rites for those who follow the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle. Then the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>, with unblinking eyes, spoke thus to the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One): 'Hear me, O <s>Bhagavat</s>! This <s>vimokṣamukhamaṇḍala</s> (circle of the gateway to liberation), which is honored by all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, is for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the great multitude of beings. Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established throughout the three times! Homage to the assemblies of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> and noble <s>Śrāvakas</s>, past, future, and present! Homage to those who have gone rightly! Homage to those who have rightly practiced! Homage to <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (Śāriputra), the great lord of generosity! Homage to the great assemblies of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> headed by the noble <s>Maitreya</s>! Homage to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and completely awakened ones, past, future, and present! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Suvarṇavarṇaprabha</s> (Golden-Colored Radiance)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Siṃhavikrīḍitarāja</s> (King of Lion's Play)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vipaśvin</s>! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śikhin</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and completely awakened one! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Viśvabhu</s>! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Krakucchanda</s>! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Kanakamuni</s>! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the noble <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and completely awakened one! The <s>dhāraṇī</s> is as follows:

body.text: om mune mune mahāmunaye svāhā / om same same mahāsame rakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvasattvānāṃca sarvapāpaprasamane svāhā // // // namaḥ suparikīrttita nāma dheyāya tathāgatāyā / namaḥ samantāvabhāsavijitasaṃgrāmaśriye tathāgatāya / namaḥ indraketudhvajaśriye tathāgatāya arhate samyaksambuddhāya / namo vikrāntagāmine tathāgatāyārhate samyaksambuddhāya / namo buddhāya namo dharmāya namaḥ saṃghāya / namo atītānāgata pratyutpannebhyo buddhebhyo bhagavadbhyaḥ // tadyathā //
body.translated_text: Oṃ <s>mune mune mahāmunaye svāhā</s>! Oṃ <s>same same mahāsame</s>, protect, protect me and all beings, O pacifier of all sins, <s>svāhā</s>! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Suparikīrtitanāmadheya</s> (He Whose Name Is Well-Proclaimed)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Samantāvabhāsavijitasaṃgrāmaśrī</s> (Glorious One Victorious in Battle Through All-Pervading Radiance)! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Indraketudhvajaśrī</s> (Glorious One with the Banner of Indra's Standard), the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and completely awakened one! Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vikrāntagāmin</s> (Heroic Strider), the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and completely awakened one! Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>! Homage to the <s>Dharma</s>! Homage to the <s>Saṅgha</s>! Homage to the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, past, future, and present! The <s>dhāraṇī</s> is as follows:

body.text:
smṛtivarddhani gativarddhani dhṛtivarddhani prajñāvarddhani pratibhānavarddhani dhyānavarddhani samaryavarddhani sarvabodhipakṣadharmmavarddhani sakalaburddhadharmaparipūṇīye svāhā // // namo ratnatrayāya namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākārūṇikāya / ebhyo namaskṛtvā idamāryāvalokiteśvaramukhoṅgīrṇamamoghapāśarājannāma hṛdayaṃ tathāgata saṃmukhabhāṣitaṃ mahatā parṣata madhye ahamidāniṃmāvarttayiṣye sidhyantu me mantrapadā sarvvakāryāṇi /
sarvabhayebhyo mama sarvasattvānāṃca rakṣā bhavatu // tadyathā //
body.translated_text:
O increaser of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), increaser of progress, increaser of <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness), increaser of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), increaser of <s>pratibhāna</s> (eloquence), increaser of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), increaser of noble attainments, increaser of all <s>bodhipakṣadharmas</s> (qualities conducive to awakening), fulfiller of all the <s>Buddhadharmas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Homage to the Three Jewels (<s>Ratnatraya</s>)! Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>, the greatly compassionate one! Having paid homage to them, I shall now recite this <s>Amoghapāśarāja</s> (King of the Infallible Lasso) <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart-dhāraṇī), which issued forth from the mouth of the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> in the presence of a great assembly. May my <s>mantra</s>-words be accomplished, may all my tasks be fulfilled!
May there be protection for me and all beings from all fears! The <s>dhāraṇī</s> is as follows:

body.text:
om cara 2 ciri 2 curū 2 mara 2 miri 2 murū 2 mahākārūṇika / sara 2 siri 2 surū 2 curū 2 ciri 2 viri 2 piri 2 miri 2 mahāpadāhasta / kala 2 kili 2 kulu 2 mahāśuddhasatvā / buddhaya 2 bodha 2 bodhi 2 bodhaya 2 kaṇa 2 kiṇi 2 kuṇu 2 paramaśuddhasattva / kara 2 kiri 2 kurū 2 mahāsthāmaprāpta // cala 2 saṃcala 2 vicala 2 eṭaṭa 2 bhara 2 bhiri 2 bhurū 2 tara 2
tiri 2 turū 2 ehi mahākārūṇika / mahāpaśupativeśadhara / dhara 2 dhiri 2 dharū 2 tara 2 sara 2 cara 2 para 2 vara 2 mara 2 lara 2 hara 2 hāhā hīhī hūhū //
body.translated_text: Oṃ <s>cara cara, ciri ciri, curū curū, mara mara, miri miri, murū murū</s>, O greatly compassionate one! <s>Sara sara, siri siri, surū surū, curū curū, ciri ciri, viri viri, piri piri, miri miri</s>, O great one with hands of power! <s>Kala kala, kili kili, kulu kulu</s>, O one of great pure being! <s>Buddhaya buddhaya, bodha bodha, bodhi bodhi, bodhaya bodhaya, kaṇa kaṇa, kiṇi kiṇi, kuṇu kuṇu</s>, O supremely pure being! <s>Kara kara, kiri kiri, kurū kurū</s>, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s> (One Who Has Attained Great Power)! <s>Cala cala, saṃcala saṃcala, vicala vicala, eṭaṭa eṭaṭa, bhara bhara, bhiri bhiri, bhurū bhurū, tara tara, tiri tiri, turū turū</s>, come, O greatly compassionate one! O wearer of the guise of <s>Mahāpaśupati</s> (the Great Lord of Beings)! <s>Dhara dhara, dhiri dhiri, dharū dharū, tara tara, sara sara, cara cara, para para, vara vara, mara mara, lara lara, hara hara, hāhā hīhī hūhū</s>!

body.text: om kāra brahmeśa dhara / dhara 2 dhiri 2 dhurū 2 tara 2 sara 2 cara 2 para 2 vara 2 hara harā rasmisahasrapratimaṇḍiśarīrā / jvela 2 tapa 2 bhāsa 2 bhrama 2 bhagavana somāditya yamavarūṇakuverabrahmendravāyuagnidhanada ṛṣi devagaṇebhyarcitacaraṇa / surū 2 curū 2 murū 2 dhurū 2 sanatkumārarudravāsavaviṣṇudhanadavāyuagni ṛṣi nāyakavināyaka / bahuvividhaveśadhara / dhara 2 dhiri 2 dhurū 2 tara 2 thara 2 dhara 2 para 2 lara 2 hara 2 yara 2 sara 2 vara 2 varadāyaka samantāvalokita lokeśvara tribhuvaneśvarasarvvaguṇa samalaṅkṛta avalokiteśvara / muhu 2 murū 2 muya 2 muṃca 2 rakṣa 2 māṃ sarvasatvānāṃca sarvabhayaibhyaḥ sarvopadravebhyaḥ sarvopasagebhyaḥ sarvagrahebhyaḥ sarvavyādhibhya / sarvaviṣebhyaḥ sarvajvarebhyaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ kāra brahmeśa dhara / dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhurū dhurū tara tara sara sara cara cara para para vara vara hara harā</s> — O one whose body is adorned with a thousand rays of light! <s>Jvela jvela tapa tapa bhāsa bhāsa bhrama bhrama</s> — O <s>Bhagavat</s>, whose feet are worshipped by <s>Soma</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Brahma</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Dhanada</s>, and the hosts of <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) and <s>devas</s> (gods)! <s>Surū surū curū curū murū murū dhurū dhurū</s> — O leader of <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Vāsava</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Dhanada</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Agni</s>, the <s>ṛṣis</s>, and <s>Vināyaka</s>! O bearer of many and varied forms! <s>Dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhurū dhurū tara tara thara thara dhara dhara para para lara lara hara hara yara yara sara sara vara vara</s> — O bestower of boons, <s>Samantāvalokita</s> (All-Seeing One), <s>Lokeśvara</s> (Lord of the World), Lord of the Three Worlds, adorned with all virtues, <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>! <s>Muhu muhu murū murū muya muya muñca muñca rakṣa rakṣa</s> — protect me and all sentient beings from all fears, from all calamities, from all afflictions, from all malevolent spirits (<s>grahas</s>), from all diseases, from all poisons, from all fevers!

body.text: evaṃ vandha vandhana tāḍana tarjjana rāja taskarāgnyūdaka viṣaśastraparimocaka // kaṇa 2
body.translated_text: Thus [protect from] binding, fettering, striking, threatening, [from dangers of] kings, thieves, fire, water, poison, and weapons, O liberator! <s>Kaṇa kaṇa</s>

body.text: kiṇi 2 kuṇu 2 cara 2 ciri 2 curū 2 indriyabalabodhyaṅgacaturāryasaṃprakāśaka // tama 2 dama 2 sama 2 masa 2 dhama 2 mahakārūṇika mahātamondhakāravidhamana ṣaḍpāramitā paripūraka // mala 2 mili 2 mulu 2 / ṭa ṭa ṭa ṭa / ṭha ṭha ṭha ṭha / ḍi ḍi ḍi ḍi / ṭu ṭu ṭu ṭu / ṭhi ṭhi ṭhi ṭhi / dhu dhu dhu dhu / eneya carmakṛtaparikara / ehe hi mahākārūṇika / īśvara maheśvara mahābhūta gaṇasaṃbhaṃjaka / kara 2 kiri 2 kurū 2 para 2 hara 2 hiri 2 vara 2 sara 2 kara 2 kaṭa 2 kiṭi 2 kuṭu 2 maṭa 2 / mahāśuddhasattva viṣayanivāsina mahākārūṇika śvetayajñopavitaratna makuṭa mālādhara / sarvajñaśirasi kṛta jaṭāmakuṭa mahādbhuta kamalālaṅkṛta karataladhyānasamādhivimokṣaṃ aprakampya bahusattva santatiparivāraka / mahākārūṇik sarvakarmābaraṇaviśodhaka / sarvajñajñānaparipūraka / sarvavyādhiparimocaka / sarvasattvān paripūraka / sarvasattvasamā svāsanakarāya namo stute svāhā // amoghāya svāhā / amoghapāśāya svāhā / ajitāya svāhā / aparājitāya svāhā / amitābhāya svāhā / amitābhasutāya svāhā / mārasainyapramarddanāya svāhā / abhayapradāya svāhā / yamāya svāhā / vijayāya svāhā / jaya vijayāya svāhā / idaṃcamekarma kara namo stute svāhā / om raṇa raṇa om phaṭ svāhā / oṃ jaya huṃ phaṭ svāha / oṃ jupi svāhā / oṃ jaya svāhā / oṃ hrīḥ trailokyavijayāmoghapāśapratihata hrīṃ haḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā / oṃ vasumati svāhā / oṃ ārolīka svāhā / oṃ bahule bahule svāhā / oṃ ārolika hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā // //
body.translated_text: <s>kiṇi kiṇi kuṇu kuṇu cara cara ciri ciri curū curū</s> — O illuminator of the <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), and the Four Noble Truths (<s>caturāryasatya</s>)! <s>Tama tama dama dama sama sama masa masa dhama dhama</s> — O Great Compassionate One (<s>mahākāruṇika</s>), dispeller of the great darkness of delusion, fulfiller of the <s>ṣaṭpāramitās</s> (six perfections)! <s>Mala mala mili mili mulu mulu / ṭa ṭa ṭa ṭa / ṭha ṭha ṭha ṭha / ḍi ḍi ḍi ḍi / ṭu ṭu ṭu ṭu / ṭhi ṭhi ṭhi ṭhi / dhu dhu dhu dhu</s> — O one wearing a girdle of deer-skin! Come, O Great Compassionate One! O <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, crusher of hosts of great beings! <s>Kara kara kiri kiri kurū kurū para para hara hara hiri hiri vara vara sara sara kara kara kaṭa kaṭa kiṭi kiṭi kuṭu kuṭu maṭa maṭa</s> — O great pure being (<s>mahāśuddhasattva</s>), dwelling in the realm [of beings], O Great Compassionate One, wearer of the white sacred thread, jewel crown, and garlands! O one with a crest of matted locks placed upon the head of omniscience, wondrously adorned with lotuses, holding in the palm meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation) unshakably, surrounded by a great retinue of many beings! O Great Compassionate One, purifier of all <s>karmāvaraṇa</s> (karmic obscurations), fulfiller of omniscient knowledge, liberator from all diseases, fulfiller of all beings, one who brings all beings to peaceful rest—homage and praise to you, <s>svāhā</s>! <s>Amoghāya svāhā / Amoghapāśāya svāhā / Ajitāya svāhā / Aparājitāya svāhā / Amitābhāya svāhā / Amitābhasutāya svāhā / Mārasainyapramardanāya svāhā / Abhayapradāya svāhā / Yamāya svāhā / Vijayāya svāhā / Jayavijayāya svāhā</s> / Accomplish this ritual of mine, homage and praise, <s>svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ raṇa raṇa oṃ phaṭ svāhā / Oṃ jaya huṃ phaṭ svāhā / Oṃ jupi svāhā / Oṃ jaya svāhā / Oṃ hrīḥ trailokyavijayāmoghapāśapratihata hrīṃ haḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā / Oṃ vasumati svāhā / Oṃ ārolīka svāhā / Oṃ bahule bahule svāhā / Oṃ ārolika hrīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

body.text: sarṣaparavadirakīlakādyaiḥ sarvajvareṣu sūtrakaṃ vandhayitavyaṃ sarvavyādhiṣu ghṛtatailamudakaṃ vā parijapya dātavyaṃ / kākhordacchedanaṃ rakṣā sūtreṇa śastreṇa udaraśūlena lavaṇodakaṃ viṣa nāśanaṃ mṛttikayā udakena vā cakṣurogena śvetasūtrakaṃ karṇe vandhayitavyaṃ / danta śūle karavīradantakāṣṭhaṃ / sīmāvandhe paṃcaraṅigakasūtrakamekaviṃśativārān parijapya catuḥṣu khadirakīleṣu vaddhvā caturddiśaṃ nikhātavyaṃ simā vandho bhavati / sarvarakṣā sūtrakena udakena bhasmakena vā sarvagraheṣu / paṃcaraṅigaka sūtrakaṃ sarvajvareṣu śvetasūtrakaṃ sarppakīṭhalūtalohaliṅgala graheṣu / madhupippalīyutaṃ cakṣuroge / gandhodakaṃ palāśodakaṃ madhūyaṣṭyudaka vā sarvakalikalaha vivādebhyaḥ ākhyāneṣu udakaṃ parijapya mukhaprakṣālayitavyaṃ / paraviṣayarājyarāṣṭrakeṣu pūrṇakalaśaṃ sthāpayitvā śūcināsūcivastraprāvṛtena mahatī pūjāṃ kṛtvā bācayitavyaṃ / mahāśānti bhavati / tena codakena sektavyaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ rakṣā kṛtā bhavati /
body.translated_text: For all fevers, a cord should be tied [on the afflicted person] using mustard seeds, <s>rāvadira</s> pegs, and the like. For all diseases, ghee, oil, or water should be consecrated [with the mantra] and given. For removing <s>kākhorda</s> (sorcery), a protective cord or a blade should be used. For stomach pain, salt-water. For destroying poison, [use] clay or water. For eye disease, a white cord should be tied on the ear. For toothache, [use] a <s>karavīra</s> (oleander) tooth-stick. For binding a boundary, a five-colored cord should be consecrated twenty-one times, tied to four <s>khadira</s> (acacia) pegs, and driven into the four directions — a boundary-binding comes into effect. For all protection, [use] a cord, water, or ash for all planetary afflictions. A five-colored cord for all fevers; a white cord for snake, insect, spider, and <s>lohaliṅgala</s> afflictions. For eye disease, [use a remedy] mixed with honey and long pepper. For all quarrels, disputes, and conflicts, and in legal cases, water should be consecrated and used to wash the face. In foreign lands, kingdoms, and realms, a full water-pot should be established, and having covered it with a clean cloth pierced with a needle, a great worship should be performed and the [mantra] should be recited. A great pacification comes about. And with that water, [the area] should be sprinkled — protection for all beings is accomplished.

body.text: sarvetyupadravopasargāḥ praśāmyanti / mudritāyā candanatilakaṃ hṛdaye ekaviṃśativārān parijapya kartavyaṃ sarvānantaryāṇi kṣayaṃ yānti / satataṃ jāpena gṛharakṣā / padma homena sarvasattvarakṣā / candanahomena sarvabhūtagraharakṣā jaya vijayā / aparājitānākulī / gandhanākūlī dhāraṇī abhayapāṇi / indriyapāṇi / gandhaḥ priyaṃgu tagaracakrā mahācakrāviṣṇukrāntā somarājī sūnandā ceti / eṣaṃ yathā saṃbhavataḥ / aṣṭottaraśatavārān parijapya maṇiṃ kṛtvā śirasi bāhau vā dhārayitavyaṃ / bālānāṃ galenārīṇāṃ vilagne svayaṃ paraṃ saubhāgyakaraṃ / maṇe lakṣmīprasamanāṃ putradaṃ ca / etena maṇivaddhena sarvarakṣā kṛtā bhavati / viṣāgninaṃ kramati /
body.translated_text: All calamities and afflictions are pacified. A <s>candana</s> (sandalwood) mark should be made on the heart [of the image] while consecrating it twenty-one times — all <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) sins are destroyed. Through constant recitation, protection of the home [is achieved]. Through a lotus <s>homa</s> (fire oblation), protection of all beings. Through a sandalwood <s>homa</s>, protection from all <s>bhūtagraha</s> (spirit-possessions) — victory and conquest. <s>Aparājitā</s> (the Unconquered), <s>Nākulī</s>, fragrant <s>Nākulī</s>, <s>Dhāraṇī</s>, <s>Abhayapāṇi</s> (Fearless-Handed), <s>Indriyapāṇi</s>, fragrance, <s>priyangu</s>, <s>tagara</s>, <s>cakrā</s>, <s>mahācakrā</s>, <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>somarājī</s>, <s>sunandā</s> — these [herbs and substances], as available. Having consecrated them one hundred and eight times, they should be made into an amulet and worn on the head or arm. For children, [tied] around the neck; for women, worn upon the body — it produces good fortune for oneself and others. The amulet [brings] the pacification of <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune) and the granting of sons. With this amulet tied on, all protection is accomplished. Poison and fire do not afflict [the wearer].

body.text: viṣakṛtatpadyate / utpannā api na pīḍāṃ janayiṣyanti / śīghraṃ prasamayiṣyanti / vātamedhāśanistaṃbhanaṃ vāriṇā karaviralatayā sarvakarmakaram // āryāvallokiteśvarahṛdayaṃ paramasiddhamasasādhita mete tāni karmmāṇi kurute / atha sādhayitumicchan dvidhiḥ / paṭe 'śleṣaṃ kairvarṇakairbuddhapratimāmālikhya āryyāvalokiśvaro jaṭāmakutadhārī eṇeya carmakṛtaparikaraḥ paśupativeśadhara sarvālaṅkāravibhūṣitaṃ kṛtvā poṣadhikena citrakareṇa citrāpayitavyaḥ / tataḥsādhakena tasyāgrataḥ gomayena maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā śvetapuṣpāvakīrṇa aṣṭāu gandhodakapūrṇakumbhāḥ sthāpayitavyāḥ / aṣṭāvupahārāaścatuḥ ṣaṣṭhirūpakaraṇāni / vali mānsaṃ ca rūdhirabarjjitaṃ agarūdhūpaṃ dahatā vidyāaṣṭamasahasraṃ jāpayitavyā / ahorātroṣitena rātroṣitena vā / triśūklabhojina triṣkālasnāpayitā śūcivastraprāvṛtto bhūtvā japā dātavyaṃ / ataḥ pratimāyā 'rpataḥ ātmānaṃ ca likhitaṃ paśyati / taddaṣṭvā ca prahṛṣyati yāvat svapnane vā āryāvalokiteśvaro āgacchati / sarvesā paripūrayati / manaḥ śilāṃ rajataṃ vā parijapya kṣīṇāṃjayitvā tatoantarhito bhavati / ākāśe krāmati / asaṃmohavyūha nāma samādhiṃ prati labhate / yadicchati tatkaroti eva sādhaka iti // //
body.translated_text: Poison that has been administered is detected. Even afflictions that have already arisen will not cause suffering. They will quickly be pacified. For stopping wind, clouds, and thunderbolts, [use] water together with an oleander branch — it accomplishes all ritual acts. The heart [-dhāraṇī] of noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> is supremely efficacious when properly accomplished; one who has accomplished it performs those ritual acts. Now, the method for one who wishes to accomplish it: On a cloth, using various pigments, one should paint a <s>Buddha</s> image together with noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> wearing a matted-hair crown, dressed in a deer-skin garment, bearing the appearance of <s>Paśupati</s> (Lord of Creatures), adorned with all ornaments — this should be painted by an artist observing the <s>poṣadha</s> (fasting) vow. Then, the practitioner, before that [image], having made a <s>maṇḍala</s> (ritual circle) with cow-dung strewn with white flowers, should place eight water-pots filled with scented water. Eight offerings and sixty-four ornamental accessories [should be arranged]. Oblation-food and flesh, excluding blood, should be offered. While burning <s>agaru</s> (aloe-wood) incense, the <s>vidyā</s> (mantra) should be recited eight thousand times. [The practitioner should be] fasting for a day and night or fasting at night, eating pure food three times, bathing three times daily, and wearing clean garments — thus the recitation should be performed. Thereupon, one sees oneself depicted before the image. Having seen that, one rejoices. Eventually, even in dreams, noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> comes and fulfills all [wishes]. Having consecrated <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) or silver, having conquered depletion, one thereby becomes invisible. One traverses the sky. One obtains the <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) called <s>Asaṃmohavyūha</s> (Array of Non-Delusion). Whatever the practitioner wishes, that indeed he accomplishes.

body.text: idamavocat bhagavānāttamanā āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattva rūteca bhikṣavarūte ca bodhisatvāste śuddhāvāsakāyikāśca devaputrāḥ sadevamānuṣāsura gandharvaścaloko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti // //
body.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. The noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, was delighted, as were those <s>bhikṣus</s> and those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and the <s>devaputras</s> of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes), and the world with its <s>devas</s>, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s> — all rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

body.text: // āryāmoghapāśahṛdayaṃ nāma mahāyāna sūtraṃ samāptas //
body.translated_text: The Noble <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s>, a <s>Mahāyāna sūtra</s>, is concluded.

children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> which arise from causes — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause;

children.text: hyavadatteṣāṃca yo nirodha evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: Indeed, their cessation is pure — thus speaks the Great Ascetic (<s>Mahāśramaṇa</s>).
